title: How strong are magnetic fields?
caption: Magnetic flux density runs from tens of microtesla (Earth, ~50 μT) to ~10¹¹ T (a magnetar), about 15 orders of magnitude. A 1.5 T MRI field is 1.5/(5 × 10⁻⁵) = 30000 times Earth's field, 4.5 orders of magnitude up.
alt: A logarithmic scale of magnetic flux density in tesla from 10^-6 to 10^12, with Earth's field, a fridge magnet, an MRI, the strongest steady laboratory field, a neutron star and a magnetar marked.
description: A horizontal logarithmic scale of magnetic flux density in tesla.

Marked from weakest to strongest: Earth's field at the surface about 50 μT, a fridge magnet about 5 mT, an MRI 1.5 T, the strongest steady laboratory field about 45 T, a neutron star about 10⁸ T and a magnetar up to about 10¹¹ T.
The MRI field is 30000 times Earth's field: 4.5 orders of magnitude.
